Bent low over an open grimoire, quill moving in tight careful strokes, left hand pressing the page flat, lips slightly parted, eyes tracking each line of script as the nib crosses vellum.
Standing at the cauldron with both hands wrapped around a long wooden stirring rod, stirring slow counterclockwise circles, face tilted toward the rising steam, brow furrowed in quiet concentration.
Seated cross-legged on the floor, a large star-chart spread across their lap, charcoal stick tracing an arc between two constellation points, free hand holding the parchment edge from curling.
Holding a faintly glowing rune-stone up toward the candlelight with both hands, head tilted back slightly, squinting, turning it a few degrees to examine the carved symbol at a new angle.
Slumped peacefully in a wide armchair, an open tome resting face-down on their chest, chin dropped, breathing slow, one hand still loosely curled around the spine as if reluctant to release it.
Crouching beside the hearth, using a thin iron tool to light the burner beneath a copper alembic, other hand shielding the flame from a draft, whole attention fixed on the fragile spark catching.
Seated at the writing desk, inking a ritual seal onto a square of fresh vellum, tongue pressed lightly to lower lip, drawing each curved segment with slow deliberate rotation of the wrist.
Measuring dried herbs one pinch at a time into a small stone mortar, leaning close to inspect the quantity, free arm resting on the worktable, face calm and methodical.
Perched on a stool before two open books laid side by side, finger moving back and forth between corresponding passages, head turning left then right, comparing the two texts in murmured silence.
Standing at the tall window in the grey morning light, both hands around a heavy clay mug, steam rising past their face, gaze drifting across the rooftops below, mind clearly elsewhere.
Kneeling on the stone floor, chalk in hand, drawing the outer ring of a large magical circle, body leaning forward, free hand occasionally smoothing a smudged line, working section by section.
Sitting at the workbench, pouring a pale green liquid from a small flask into a narrow glass vial held up at eye level, other hand steadying the flask spout, moving with practiced care.
Hunched over a parchment scroll unrolled across the desk, using a magnifying lens on a short handle to examine a faded passage, shoulders rounded, nose nearly touching the glass.
Seated sideways in the armchair with legs draped over one arm, reading a slim volume held above their face, free hand absently pulling at a loose thread on their robe hem.
Coaxing a small candle flame slowly higher with one open hand held a few inches above it, watching the flame lean and stretch toward the palm, expression intent, barely breathing.
At the writing desk in candlelight, pausing mid-sentence with quill lifted, staring at the half-finished line, one hand pressed to the cheek, thinking before committing the next word to the page.
Grinding dried petals in the mortar with a slow rolling motion of the pestle, leaning over the bench, occasionally pausing to pinch a bit between two fingers and test the texture.
Holding a cloudy glass orb carefully in both cupped hands, seated at the desk, elbows planted, turning it very slowly and studying the faint light shifting inside its depths.
Sketching a star-chart at the drafting table, ruler held in place by one forearm while the other hand draws fine position lines, a reference scroll pinned open beside the work.

Dipping a finger into the simmering cauldron liquid, pulling it back quickly, then rubbing the finger against the thumb to feel the consistency, face thoughtful, already reaching for the next ingredient.
Mending a torn page with a thin thread of pale light drawn slowly along the tear from fingertip, other hand pressing the two edges gently together, bending close to guide the seam.
Asleep at the writing desk, head resting on crossed forearms, quill still loosely held in one limp hand, the unfinished grimoire entry visible beneath their elbow, a candle burning low.
Standing at the high bookshelf on a short ladder, running a finger slowly along the spines of aged volumes, pulling one halfway out then pushing it back, searching for the right text.
Seated at the bench, using a magnifying glass to inspect a small glowing crystal, tilting it with one careful fingertip against the cloth underneath, noting something in a margin with the other hand.
Levitating a small bundle of dried herbs a few inches above an open flask, holding one hand flat beneath it, lips moving in quiet murmur, watching the oils slowly release into the rising warmth.
